I'm writing this article just before heading off on a short trip up north. Every time I leave home, there are a few essential devices in my smart home system that I rely on completely to make sure everything runs smoothly. A quick reminder: to control your devices remotely and use all the features below, you need a dedicated Apple Home hub, such as an Apple TV 4K or HomePod.

The "HomeKit Weekly" series covers smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything related to the Apple smart home framework.

Outdoor watering system automation

Where I live, the weather gets unbearably hot. I'd say when you're not home, you're definitely hoping for rain—otherwise you'll have to water things yourself. If you're travelling during the summer, automatic watering is absolutely one of the simplest and most practical smart home applications. If you've ever come back from a week away to find a patch of lawn or a few potted plants completely dead, you'll understand exactly what I mean. There are plenty of smart products on the market that connect directly to your tap, allowing you to turn on sprinklers manually or set up automations based on specific times and local weather conditions.

Walk into a comfortable temperature the moment you get home

Coming home from a long trip to a house that's hot and stuffy, with the air conditioning taking forever to cool down—that feeling is the worst. But on the other hand, running the air conditioning for a long time just to maintain a set temperature in an empty house is really too wasteful. If you use a smart thermostat that supports Apple Home, you can remotely adjust the air conditioning to your preferred temperature the night before. I've been using this method for several years. I like to run the air conditioning at night so the unit can bring the temperature back down during the coolest part of the day. This saves money while also reducing unnecessary wear on the air conditioner.

Automatically turning lights on and off to create the illusion of someone being home

One of the most traditional anti-theft methods is to leave a few lights on so the house looks occupied. The problem is, if the same light stays on day and night, you're basically telling people on the street that nobody's home. This is where Apple Home really comes into its own. Set up automations for a few of your main lights, and you can control them manually from afar, or set random schedules to truly create the effect of someone moving around the house.

Monitor your home with HomeKit cameras

When I'm travelling, of course I don't want to worry about home all the time, but I do genuinely want to know if anything's happening. In fact, last year while I was on a trip, it was thanks to a single notification that I spotted a small problem right away. That's why I trust HomeKit Secure Video so much. I've set up several cameras around the outside of my home to keep an eye on the surroundings. With HomeKit Secure Video, all recordings are stored securely on iCloud+, and since I also use two Apple TVs as hubs, I can view live footage and recorded clips anytime, anywhere, as long as I have a network connection.

Wrapping up

Summer is a great time to travel, but extreme heat also means you need to keep a closer eye on home. With the right Apple Home setup, you can keep your lawn watered, walk into a cool house, have your lights turn on and off at irregular times, and check live camera feeds from anywhere. These are exactly the setups I use when I'm away on business or when the family goes on a trip, and they really do make the journey much easier.
